> Curated papers, systems, tools, and benchmarks for AI-assisted scientific discovery.

AI agents can propose scientific hypotheses, write and run experimental code, and turn research records into manuscripts. This collection examines systems such as [Google Co-Scientist](docs/systems.md#google-co-scientist-system), [Agentic Scientist](docs/systems.md#agentic-scientist-system), and [DiscoveryRSI](docs/systems.md#discoveryrsi-system): how they work, what they produce, and what their evaluations establish. Compare available code, inspect benchmark results and observed failures, and use evaluation guides to design your own studies.

[Browse papers](docs/papers.md) · [Compare systems](docs/capability-matrix.md) · [Read local experiments](docs/reproducibility.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Selected reading

Selected resources, newest first. Year-only entries follow dated entries within each year; all catalogs retain topic indexes.

| Date | Resource / status | Summary & evidence | Links |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;13</code> | [The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18933)<br>*preprint* | Coordinates coding agents through task drafting, ideas, sandboxed experiments, baselines, ablations, analysis, and manuscript writing. A meta-controller enforces stage-specific rubrics. The paper reports computational discovery studies and an ALIFE 2026 paper produced in a co-scientist setting; that human collaboration should be distinguished from its separate autonomous evaluations. | [Details](docs/papers.md#agentic-scientist) |
| <code>2026&#8209;09&#8209;17</code> | [ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19644)<br>*preprint* | Starts from a research problem, establishes baselines, proposes hypotheses, runs experiments and ablations, and iterates through simulated reviews. Evaluation includes publication-derived machine-learning tasks, integrity audits, automated reviewers, and a human study of generated papers. These complementary author-reported assessments remain bounded by the selected tasks; simulated acceptance is distinct from actual venue acceptance. | [Details](docs/papers.md#scientist-two) |
| <code>2026&#8209;09&#8209;15</code> | [ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523)<br>*preprint* | Turns researcher requests, feedback, and execution traces into learning tasks and evaluation rubrics. An inner loop adapts the agent harness while an outer loop trains the model under the improved harness. Case studies cover four scientific task families; they demonstrate the proposed learning workflow rather than universal autonomous discovery. | [Details](docs/papers.md#sciencebuddy) |
| <code>2026&#8209;07&#8209;03</code> | [ResearchStudio](https://github.com/microsoft/ResearchStudio)<br>*preprint* | Microsoft's research skill collection includes Idea for developing literature-grounded research proposals and Reel for turning completed papers into posters, narrated videos, blogs, and interactive presentations. The code exposes editable workflows for coding agents. Its two modules support different stages of research and communication; their presence does not establish an autonomous experimental discovery pipeline. | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04439) · [Details](docs/tools.md#researchstudio-tool) |
| <code>2026&#8209;05&#8209;25</code> | [ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340)<br>*preprint* | Maintains explicit evidence chains from literature and experiments to manuscript claims, with audits for score reproduction, specification violations, references, and method-code agreement. The authors compare generated papers across research tasks and report improved integrity. These are task-specific audits, so the title's human-level claim should not be generalized to all research. | [Details](docs/papers.md#scientist-one) |
| <code>2026&#8209;05&#8209;19</code> | [Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10644-y)<br>*peer reviewed* | Uses specialized agents to generate, criticize, rank, and evolve hypotheses through tournaments, with scientists setting goals and steering exploration. The Nature paper includes biomedical applications and laboratory validation of selected hypotheses. The system supports scientific reasoning; experimental validation remains a distinct process rather than an automatically closed physical loop. | [Details](docs/papers.md#google-co-scientist) |
| <code>2026&#8209;04&#8209;06</code> | [PaperOrchestra](https://github.com/google-research/paper-orchestra)<br>*preprint* | Transforms research ideas, experimental records, and formatting requirements into LaTeX manuscripts through specialized planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. The official Google Research repository accompanies the paper and evaluation resources. It addresses synthesis of existing research materials; manuscript quality ratings do not verify that the underlying experiments or scientific conclusions are correct. | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018) · [Details](docs/tools.md#paperorchestra-tool) |
| <code>2026</code> | [OpenResearch](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch)<br>*project* | A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark. | [Details](docs/systems.md#openresearch-system) |
| <code>2025&#8209;04&#8209;02</code> | [PaperBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01848)<br>*peer reviewed* | Asks agents to implement and execute replications of 20 ICML 2024 papers from scratch. Author-developed hierarchical rubrics divide the work into 8,316 gradable items, with a separately assessed model-based grader. Scores indicate progress toward specified replication requirements; code-only variants, partial rubric credit, and successful empirical replication must be distinguished. | [Code](https://github.com/openai/frontier-evals) · [Details](docs/benchmarks.md#paperbench) |
| <code>2024&#8209;10&#8209;07</code> | [ScienceAgentBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05080)<br>*peer reviewed* | Contains 102 expert-validated tasks derived from 44 publications across four disciplines. Each task requires a self-contained Python program, assessed through code, execution outputs, and costs. The benchmark deliberately tests individual data-driven research steps, providing a stronger basis for bounded capability claims than treating generated manuscripts as evidence of complete scientific discovery. | [Code](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench) · [Details](docs/benchmarks.md#scienceagentbench) |

## Scope

We include systems that formulate hypotheses, conduct experiments, analyse results, or communicate scientific findings. Supporting tools and benchmarks are included when their role in these activities is explicit. General-purpose agents require a concrete connection to scientific research.

<a id="how-to-read-the-evidence"></a>

**Preprint**, **peer-reviewed**, and **project** identify source status. Peer review requires a linked publication record; project entries describe official documentation. **Content checked** records source inspection, not execution. Missing code links indicate unconfirmed availability.

Proposal ratings, successful execution, and validated discoveries measure different outcomes. Comparisons therefore retain the task, budget, human roles, and evaluation setting. Our local reports cover selected components; they do not reproduce complete research campaigns or published scientific findings.

## Recent additions

Eight recent works, with one row per work and links to each catalog entry. Ordered by addition date; the Date column shows publication or release.

| Date | Resource / status | Summary & evidence | Links |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;03</code> | [From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-05 | Pairs persistent and reset instances of fixed-model research agents across nine task families, measuring initial solutions, search efficiency, and final hidden-test performance. Persistent state helps five agents reach useful solutions sooner, but final gains vary and stricter initialization controls remove the general search advantage. Relevant versus shuffled insight cards also yield mixed effects. Short task streams, mostly single matched runs, and native-scaffold differences limit claims of continual scientific learning. | [Details](docs/papers.md#continual-autoresearch) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;02</code> | [Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03543)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-05 | Tests expert-guided translation, baseline reconstruction, and feedback-driven invention of differentiable warm-rain parameterizations against superdroplet simulations. Unattended experiments span ten models; two of 100 refined closures outperform the strongest retuned physical scheme on held-out rain-mass error. Most median feedback gains lack statistical significance, and retuned physical baselines remain competitive. Evidence concerns one isolated process, without coupled climate-model validation; expert effort varies substantially across tasks. | [Details](docs/papers.md#earth-system-parameterization-agents) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;02</code> | [Cloudra: Geometric Reasoning and Scientific Validation for Autonomous Reaction Mechanism Exploration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02909)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-05 | Constrains multi-agent reaction-mechanism exploration through species and reaction-step objects carrying geometries, molecular identities, and calculation evidence. Deterministic geometry tools, frequency checks, and intrinsic reaction coordinates test the proposed connections. Same-model workflow comparisons cover 50 small-molecule tasks. Published scores use human-organized records from each run, with one run per task and configuration; electronic-energy and pathway checks do not establish experimental mechanisms or solution-phase free energies. | [Code](https://github.com/yyywaa/Cloudra-mechanism-agent) · [Paper details](docs/papers.md#cloudra) · [Benchmark details](docs/benchmarks.md#cloudrabench) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;02</code> | [ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03238)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-04 | Converts scientific-software documentation into procedural skills and lookup references, then uses execution failures to propose and validate library revisions. Evolution tasks are separate from final evaluation, where the library is frozen. Tests span six scientific applications with model-based and native-agent protocols. Reported gains concern bounded software-operation tasks; evaluator repairs, application-specific effects, and different resource-access rules matter when comparing results. | [Code](https://github.com/HSZD-Team/ScienceCUA) · [Paper details](docs/papers.md#sciencecua) · [Benchmark details](docs/benchmarks.md#scienceboard-ve) |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;28</code> | [Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38691)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-04 | Audits research-agent judgments and labels numerical claims to distinguish missing artifact support from values attributed to the wrong experiment, metric, or run. A deterministic checker scores contextual provenance and tests nearby numerical decoys, with held-out human annotation. Its high-precision certification covers only a subset of claims; failure to verify does not establish falsehood, and traceability does not establish the experiment’s scientific validity. | [Code](https://github.com/mos3b-faqeeh/agent-integrity-analysis) · [Paper details](docs/papers.md#misattributed-numbers) · [Tool details](docs/tools.md#claim-evidence-checker) |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;27</code> | [OpenFrontiers-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37739)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-04 | Provides 200 mathematics problems with Lean statements, separating recently resolved problems from a still-open track. Published agent evaluations use the 50-item HQ subset under closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions. Formal solutions must pass two checkers. Statement reviews are performed by AI agents; typing checks alone do not validate mathematical meaning. Live-web success largely reflects solution retrieval, and open-item acceptances require statement review before novelty claims. | [Details](docs/benchmarks.md#openfrontiers-bench) |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;29</code> | [Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40589)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-02 | Coordinates question selection, theoretical derivation, computational checks, and nitrogen-vacancy spin experiments through agents that can reject or revise collaborators’ work. An acquisition agreeing with predictions was classified inconclusive after drift controls failed; a revised protocol passed the retained criteria. Evidence comes from one configured laboratory investigation. Humans assembled the apparatus and configured safety limits; internal agent checks do not constitute independent replication. | [Details](docs/papers.md#collaborative-quantum-spin-lab) |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;27</code> | [VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37923)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-02 | Converts perovskite-solar-cell papers into structured device records using versioned annotation and verification policies, then supports evidence-gated analyses and temporal performance prediction. Expert audits calibrate verifier agreement, while deployment reliability is estimated by model judges, including one sharing the generator’s backbone. Each record represents a paper’s best device. One-domain retrospective associations and a held-out publication year do not establish causal design rules or prospective discovery. | [Code](https://github.com/jiayijdong/VerifiedLab) · [Details](docs/papers.md#verifiedlab) |

## Curation and daily updates

Daily curation checks primary sources for new work and project changes. We publish substantive additions and corrections after validation. See the [search protocol](docs/search-protocol.md) for coverage limits and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for updates; coverage is not exhaustive.

This collection is AI-assisted and maintainer-owned. Automated checks validate catalog structure and generated files; scientific claims require source review.

## Contributing

Suggest a [resource or correction](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-ai-co-scientist/issues/new?template=resource.yml), report a [reproduction attempt](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-ai-co-scientist/issues/new?template=reproduction.yml), or share [practical experience](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-ai-co-scientist/issues/new?template=experience.yml). Include sources, methods, and limitations; failed attempts are welcome. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [open contribution topics](docs/community-roadmap.md).

The catalogs in [data/](data/) generate the indexes. The [data reference](docs/data-reference.md) explains their structure and reuse. Cite primary papers for scientific claims; use [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) and a commit ID when citing this collection.
